epithet: “We feed you only for the Face of Allah”
lede: The surah of every Friday dawn. It asks the human being to remember the long age in which he was nothing at all, and then spends most of its length on a single portrait: the righteous, what they did, and what was made ready for them.

names.name: al-Insān
names.note: After the human being named in its first ayah, and the name it carries in the muṣḥaf.

names.name: Hal Atā
names.note: Its opening words, and the name it has in the hadith: the Prophet ﷺ used to recite Hal atā ʿalā l-insān in the dawn prayer on Fridays (Muslim 879).

names.name: al-Dahr
names.note: After the “stretch of time” of its first ayah. Ibn al-Jawzī heads it with this name.

revelation.detail: Ibn al-Jawzī gives three views. That all of it is Madinan — the saying of the majority, Mujāhid and Qatādah among them. That it is Makkan — the saying of Ibn Yasār and Muqātil, and reported from Ibn ʿAbbās; Ibn Kathīr gives it as Makkan. And that it is part one and part the other. Al-Qurṭubī records the same difference. The muṣḥaf heads it Madinan, and the traditional order places it ninety-eighth; but its manner — short ayat, the next life, patience under the taunts of the disbelievers — is that of the Makkan surahs around it.
revelation.when: Madinah, on the majority’s view; Makkah, on that of Ibn Kathīr and others

evidence.quote: وَفِيها ثَلاثَةُ أقْوالٍ. أحَدُها: أنَّها مَدَنِيَّةٌ كُلُّها، قالَهُ الجُمْهُورُ مِنهُمْ، مُجاهِدٌ وقَتادَةُ. والثّانِي: مَكِّيَّةٌ، قالَهُ ابْنُ يَسارٍ، ومُقاتِلٌ، وحُكِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ. والثّالِثُ: أنَّ فِيها مَكِّيًّا ومَدَنِيًّا
وَهِيَ إِحْدَى وَثَلَاثُونَ آيَةً مَكِّيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وَمُقَاتِلٍ وَالْكَلْبِيِّ. وَقَالَ الْجُمْهُورُ: مَدَنِيَّةٌ

attested.quote: سُورَةُ الْإِنْسَانِ قَالَ عَطَاءٌ: هِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ وَقَالَ مُجَاهِدٌ وَقَتَادَةُ: مَدَنِيَّةٌ وَقَالَ الْحَسَنُ وَعِكْرِمَةُ: هِيَ مَدَنِيَّةٌ إِلَّا آيَةً
attested.says: ʿAṭāʾ said: Makkan. Mujāhid and Qatādah said: Madinan. Al-Ḥasan and ʿIkrimah said: Madinan, except one ayah.

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ النَّحّاسُ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ الإنْسانِ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by al-Naḥḥās.
Madinan, in the saying of the majority.

setting: No occasion is soundly reported for the surah as a whole. What is certain is where the Prophet ﷺ placed it in the life of his community: in the first unit of the dawn prayer every Friday he recited al-Sajdah, and in the second, this surah. The two together tell the story of the human being from first to last — creation, the test, the Hour, the two abodes — on the morning of the day on which, he said, Ādam was created and the Hour will come.

It begins before the beginning. Has there not passed over man a stretch of time in which he was not a thing worth mention? Then: a drop of mingled fluid, made to hear and see, shown the way, and left to be grateful or ungrateful. The ungrateful get one ayah. The rest of the page belongs to the others.

The description of them is the most extended picture of Paradise in the Qurʾan, and it is tied at every point to what they did. They kept their vows. They feared a Day whose evil spreads far. And they gave food, though they loved it themselves, to the poor, the orphan and the captive — saying, not aloud but in their hearts, as Mujāhid and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explained: “We feed you only for the Face of Allah. We want from you neither reward nor thanks.”
The captive, in the Arabia of the time, was an idolater taken in war. Feeding him was not owed to him as a brother in faith. It was done for the sake of Allah alone.
aim: To remind man of his origin, the purpose of his creation and his end in the two abodes — and to display the bliss of Paradise, steadying the believers and calling the disbelievers.
themes: Feeding the poor, the orphan and the captive

outline.title: From nothing, to a choice
outline.summary: Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing mentioned? We created him from a drop of mingled fluid, to test him, and made him hearing and seeing. We showed him the way: grateful, or ungrateful. For the disbelievers We have prepared chains, shackles and a blaze.

outline.title: The righteous, and what they did
outline.summary: The righteous will drink from a cup flavoured with camphor — a spring from which the servants of Allah drink, making it flow as they please. They fulfil their vows and fear a Day whose harm is widespread. They give food, despite their love of it, to the needy, the orphan and the captive: “We feed you only for the Face of Allah; we want from you neither reward nor thanks.” So Allah has shielded them from the evil of that Day, and given them radiance and joy, and rewarded them, for their patience, with a garden and silk.

outline.title: What is prepared for them
outline.summary: Reclining there on couches, seeing neither burning sun nor biting cold; its shade close over them and its fruit hung low. Vessels of silver passed among them, and goblets of crystal — crystal of silver. A cup flavoured with ginger, from a spring named Salsabīl. Youths who never age, like scattered pearls. When you look there, you see delight and a great kingdom. Garments of green silk and brocade, bracelets of silver, and a pure drink given them by their Lord. “This is your reward; your striving has been accepted.”

outline.title: To the Prophet ﷺ
outline.summary: It is We who have sent down the Qurʾan to you in stages. So be patient for your Lord’s judgement, and do not obey any sinner or ingrate among them. Remember the name of your Lord morning and evening; prostrate to Him in the night, and glorify Him through the long night.

outline.title: The choice, again
outline.summary: These people love the fleeting life and leave behind them a heavy Day. We created them and made firm their frame. This is a reminder: let whoever wills take a way to his Lord. And you do not will unless Allah wills. He admits whom He wills into His mercy; and for the wrongdoers He has prepared a painful punishment.

keyAyah.why: The definition of sincerity, in the mouths of those who have it: nothing wanted back, not even thanks.

virtues.text: The Prophet ﷺ used to recite, in the dawn prayer on Friday, “Alif Lām Mīm, the sending down” — al-Sajdah — and “Has there come upon man”.

before: Al-Qiyāmah ended with man as a drop of fluid, and asked whether its Maker cannot raise the dead. Al-Insān begins there and goes on to what he is raised for.
after: Al-Insān dwells on the reward of the righteous and gives the deniers a line. Al-Mursalāt reverses the proportion: ten times it says, “Woe, that Day, to the deniers.”

notable.label: A time when man was nothing mentioned
“We feed you only for the Face of Allah”
You do not will unless Allah wills
